title: HII Signs Shipbuilding Robotics Deal Worth $900M
summary: Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII) announced on August 6, 2026 long-term, performance-based production agreements under which it intends to award up to $900 million in shipbuilding work over seven years to Path Robotics and GrayMatter Robotics. Path provides physical-AI robotic welding technology (including Rove, which pairs its Obsidian model with a legged robot to weld directly on large ship assemblies outside fixed cells), while GrayMatter supplies robotic sanding systems. The agreements sit under HII's HYPR (High-Yield Production Robotics) program, launched in April 2026, and unfold in two stages: a Navy-grade development stage to validate high-precision welding, grinding, blasting, painting, assembly and inspection techniques, followed by a delivery stage where HII sources real production work contingent on cost, schedule and quality performance. HII said it plans to outsource more than 2.5 million hours of shipbuilding work in 2026, up 30% from 2025.
whyItMatters: Shipbuilding is one of the most complex, low-volume manufacturing environments in existence, and HII's willingness to commit up to $900 million on a performance basis is a strong signal that physical-AI robots (not just fixed-cell industrial arms) are being trusted with mission-critical work for aircraft carriers, submarines and other U.S. Navy platforms. It also illustrates a broader shift in defense manufacturing toward outsourcing fabrication to specialized automation partners rather than building all robotics capability in-house.
